done_when: The synced Forge skill tells the agent, the first time each of these happens for a person, to add one plain sentence saying what just happened and what they can do next: a story plan shown for approval, a cold read finding, a part starting, a pull request ready, a merge, a prototype demo, sign-off; never repeating it, never naming commands unless asked; a test checks each moment through forge sync and forge init

findings.body: The cold-read sentence says what the agent will do, but gives the person no next step. The merge and prototype-demo sentences likewise describe what happened without saying what the person can do next (lines 83–84). An agent following these examples would miss the stated requirement for three of the seven moments. Give each example a concrete next action for the person.
findings.title: Not done: coaching examples give the person a next step at every moment

findings.body: The test runs both Forge commands, but its per-moment assertions check only that each label has a quoted example without backticks or the text `forge `. Replacing an example with `"OK."` would still pass, although the named coaching behavior is broken. Assert that each delivered example tells the person what happened and what they can do next, and that it remains one plain sentence.
findings.title: Not done: the sync/init test verifies each coaching sentence's next step

why: People using Forge through the agent don't learn how Forge works, because the agent does each step without telling them what just happened or what they can do next
